final_answer.key_evidence_summary: Symptom-side pointer: alert on entry_service=frontend, POST /cart/checkout -> 500 Internal Server Error. Object layer read clean (all 11 deployments 1/1, pods 2/2 Running with 0 restarts, all Service endpoints bound, nodes Ready, kubelet/kube-proxy/containerd active, TCP connectivity to checkoutservice:5050 / productcatalogservice:3550 / shippingservice:50051 / paymentservice:50051 all succeeded), so the break is in the call chain's business layer. Fault carrier localized: the checkoutservice Deployment alone is generation 2 / revision 2 (patched ~3 min after namespace creation, rolling to new ReplicaSet checkoutservice-7fc85cc97b at 14:18:26Z) while every peer Deployment is generation 1, and only its pod-template hash is rewritten cycle after cycle (5b97d6df88 -> 7c8866657f -> 69f4f6cf47 -> 67f658f855 -> 7fc85cc97b); the two ReplicaSets' pod templates are otherwise byte-identical (image/env/probes/resources), so the change is inside the image code, not the manifest. Code face (break): checkoutservice/main.go getUserCart discards the required parameter (userID = "") before calling cartservice.GetCart. Runtime closure: cartservice logs 'GetCartAsync called with userId=' (empty) exactly at each PlaceOrder (e.g. 22:20:54.892814 [PlaceOrder] user_id=2119da0a-... -> 22:20:54.893637 GetCartAsync called with userId= -> 22:20:54.901885 EmptyCartAsync called with userId=2119da0a-...), and GetErrorLogs(cartservice) reports exactly this pattern as the namespace's only error group (185 lines, 9.97%). Hence checkout is executed against an empty/anonymous cart while the real user's cart is emptied, and the checkout path returns failures that surface as HTTP 500 on POST /cart/checkout at the frontend.
